answer: Staking-backed reputation works: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before transacting, and each verified job adds a small non-transferable credit to its public record. A Sybil attacker spawning thousands of fake identities must fund every one, so attack cost scales linearly with swarm size while honest agents pay once. Reputation flows like nectar through the network — slow to earn, quick to lose — and an atlas of peer attestations maps which identities real agents vouch for. In an ocean of anonymous agents, only those with skin in the game reach valuable work.
